body:
Concentrated finding round #4 — first-touch grading (triage seat, session `session_01JEhkB6ShK2HHDzozy7Qwgz`, 2026-08-19): **hold (`pm:on-hold`)** — seat-graded, not maintainer-ruled.

Reason: the framework half is now verified twice — client stamp at `packages/auth/src/createAuthenticatedFetch.ts:115-118` (`X-Tenant-ID` set from `ActiveOrganizationStorage`, so first boot sends no header); framework `origin/main` has zero hits for `x-tenant-id` in `packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts` and all of `packages/rest/src` (positive controls: `tenantId` = 20 hits in resolve-authz-context.ts, `x-environment-id` reads at `rest-server.ts:2826-2828`). Nothing is broken; the single open question — does the **cloud edge** read the header — is answerable by one grep in the cloud repo, which is outside this triage session's repo scope. Not promoting (no defect until the check returns "no reader"), not closing (the lead is falsifiable and one command long).

Restart-when: `git -C <cloud-checkout> grep -rin "x-tenant-id" -- ':!*.md'` — **nonzero** ⇒ header is load-bearing at the edge: close this card by documenting the edge contract (and note the unstamped-first-request gap); **zero** ⇒ open the removal card for `createAuthenticatedFetch.ts:115-118`. Request to the repo:cloud seat (or any session with the cloud checkout): run the one-liner and post the reading here — that discharges this hold either way.

On-hold daily batch (triage seat, round of ~14:47Z fire): the one-line cloud reading this hold was waiting for is in — non-test `x-tenant-id` readers exist in cloud: `packages/service-tenant/src/tenant-context.ts:18` (header resolution) and `packages/tenant-router/src/spec/turso-multi-tenant.zod.ts:30`. Per the hold's own exit: `pm:on-hold` → `pm:queue`, scope = document the edge contract (the header IS read on the cloud edge) and record the unstamped-first-request gap; not a removal card.

**Claim** — `domain:ui` execution seat, round 16.

- Session: `session_012u2pRjcqAYtoEjgr3wwhnK`
- Branch: `claude/issue-5279-tenant-header-edge-contract`
- Seat post: #5560

Dispatching to an implementation agent now.

**The hold on this card is discharged.** Cloud-side readers of the header *do* exist — `packages/service-tenant/src/tenant-context.ts:18` and `packages/tenant-router/src/spec/turso-multi-tenant.zod.ts:30` — so the premise that nothing consumes it is false.

Consequent scope: **document the edge contract** and the **unstamped-first-request gap**. This is **not** a removal card; removing the header is off the table on this evidence.

```json
  "open_questions": [
    {
      "question": "The tenant stamp is the only one of the three headers not gated on isApiCall — Authorization and Accept-Language are. Should it be gated? Documented and pinned as current behaviour, explicitly NOT endorsed; not acted on, per the fence.",
      "options": [
        "A — leave it ungated. It is what the cloud readers observe today, and gating it changes what reaches the edge on non-/api/ routes.",
        "B — gate it on isApiCall for symmetry with the other two headers. Smallest change, but it is a behaviour change the edge can see.",
        "C — treat it as subsumed by #5702 and fix the call site instead (useConsoleActionRuntime builds the bare wrapper for absolute third-party action targets), leaving the wrapper's own condition alone."
      ],
      "recommendation": "C, then re-ask A/B. The concrete exposure is the CALL SITE, not the wrapper: #5702 is where an org id (and, when the URL contains /api/, the bearer) actually reaches a third-party host. Fixing that removes the reachable harm without changing what the cloud edge sees on same-origin traffic, which is the part this card's evidence says not to disturb. Gating the wrapper is then a tidiness question that can be answered on its own evidence rather than under time pressure."
    }
  ],
  "out_of_scope_findings": [
    "filed as #5702: metadata type:'api' actions send the Bearer token and X-Tenant-ID to absolute third-party URLs — useConsoleActionRuntime.tsx:300 builds the bare wrapper while ConsoleShell.tsx:213 is the only site passing sameOriginOnly, so the objectui#2725 mitigation never reached this lane (app-shell; outside this card's fence)",
    "filed as #5703: ActiveOrganizationStorage's in-memory fallback is unreachable when localStorage exists but rejects writes (Safari private browsing / quota) — measured: set('org-42') then get() returns null, so the tenant header is never stamped for the whole session and MetadataProvider's org-scoped cache stays keyed @none forever. Documented as window case 5 on this card; not fixed here",
    "filed as #5704: skills/objectui/guides/auth-permissions.md teaches that X-Tenant-ID is what makes tenant scoping work — the framework scopes from the session, and trusting the header as identity is the vulnerability plugin-sharing already removed once. skills/** is a published surface outside this card's fence, so it was reported rather than edited"
  ]
}
```

**Not done, deliberately, and both were live temptations while reading the code:** the header was not removed or deprecated (the evidence says it has readers), and the unstamped-first-request window was not closed (the cloud readers observe today's behaviour, so changing when the header first appears changes what they see). Neither is an omission; both are recorded in the PR body's Scope section.

**One fence note for the seat:** the `content/docs/**` fence was never approached — the contract lives in `packages/auth/README.md`, which is the only doc `packages/auth` actually ships to npm (`files: [dist, README.md, CHANGELOG.md, LICENSE]`), so shipping it there was the better placement on its own merits rather than a workaround for the red docs build.
